title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-emily-zhou
content:
High-level: debugging recurring model load failures in production (dedicated pool) where loader fails validating weights shards. Notes + commands I ran, error snippets, quick hypotheses and next steps.

Summary of incident:
- Time window: 2026-02-19 03:10-03:40 UTC (multiple attempts from different hosts).
- Symptom: loader crashes during checkpoint assembly with checksum/size mismatch on one shard. Other requests for same model sometimes succeed.
- Affects: dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (us-west-2), model: rwd-13b-quant-v2.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- loader.py stack (truncated):
  File "/app/serving/loader.py", line 412, in load_checkpoint
    validate_shard(shard_path, expected_checksum)
  File "/app/serving/loader.py", line 176, in validate_shard
    raise ValueError(f"checksum mismatch for {shard_name} (expected {expected}, got {actual})")
ValueError: checksum mismatch for weights-00003.bin (expected 3b7f4a9d..., got 8f2c1d7b...)

- S3 client trace while fetching shard:
  botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (NoSuchKey) when calling the HeadObject operation: Not Found
  OR sometimes a partial download: socket.timeout: READ_TIMEOUT
  curl shows HTTP/1.1 200 OK but content-length smaller than expected.

Commands I ran locally on a repro host:
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/rwd-13b-quant-v2/weights-00003.bin /tmp/weights-00003.bin --region us-west-2 --no-progress
- sha256sum /tmp/weights-00003.bin  # got 8f2c1d7b... (mismatch)
- aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key rwd-13b-quant-v2/weights-00003.bin --query Metadata  # manifest says sha256=3b7f4a9d...
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/rwd-13b-quant-v2/weights-00003.bin /tmp/weights-00003.bin --expected-size 1073741824  # some attempts failed with timed out
- curl -v -H "Range: bytes=0-" https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/rwd-13b-quant-v2/weights-00003.bin -o /tmp/weights-00003.bin  # multiple runs show variable sizes (suggests partial reads)

What I observed:
- The object exists in S3 (head-object is OK most times) but occasionally returns NoSuchKey from some hosts (region-replicas?), and some GETs return truncated content.
- Sha256 from downloaded file != manifest.
- Re-downloading several times sometimes yields the correct file (rare), but often gets same corrupted/truncated file.
- Instance-level network errors observed in cloud provider logs around same time (transient network blips).

Quick repro attempt on staging:
- Brought up a pod in same AZ as failing host, repeatedly fetched all shards in parallel (8x). After ~30 attempts, got 2 corrupted shards at varying offsets.
- Single-threaded serial download appears more reliable.

Hypotheses:
1) Corruption during upload (multipart upload incomplete / missing part) -> manifest inconsistent with stored object. But head-object shows expected size/metadata, so less likely.
2) Transient S3/network issues causing truncated/partial GETs (client-side timeouts or intermediate proxies). Parallel downloads increase chance of partial reads.
3) Bug in our downloader that retries but writes partial file without truncation/atomic replace. E.g., if download fails mid-write we might leave a smaller file and subsequent checksum check reads that smaller file.
4) Race between model publish (new version) and clients reading manifest + shards -> manifest points to new checksums but some shard keys are still propagating.
5) Edge case with certain instances using IPv6 path / different CDN edge which has stale or corrupted cache.

Commands / quick fixes tried during incident:
- Restarted loader process (no effect).
- Forced re-download: rm /var/lib/weights/rwd-13b-*/weights-00003.bin && restart-loader -> transiently fixed for some hosts.
- Increased download retries in runtime to 10 and added sleep backoff -> reduced frequency but did not eliminate.
- Switched parallelism from 8 -> 2 for downloads during checkpoint assemble -> immediate reduction in failures on staging repro.

Immediate mitigation ideas (short term):
- Make downloads atomic: write to tmp file and move into place only on successful checksum verify. (we should already do this; audit code path)
- Add a final HEAD and size/etag/metadata check after download before checksum verify to catch partial writes earlier.
- Reduce parallelism for initial download stage as a safe default (configurable per-model).
- Implement server-side pre-warming or keep copies on local disk on dedicated nodes for hot models.

Longer-term fixes / infra changes:
- Ensure uploader stores a manifest with per-shard sha256 and object-etag in metadata; use s3-server-side checksum headers where possible (Content-MD5 / checksum algorithm).
- Add upload-time verification for multipart uploads: verify assembled object checksum and store result in manifest. Add CI check on model publishing.
- Improve observability: record expected vs actual size/checksum in the loader logs and ship to tracing (span events) so we can correlate per-request.
- Implement integrity-validated cache layer in front of S3 (checksums + TTL) for dedicated pools.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the model publish pipeline? (tagging Jordan for follow-up)
- Is there S3 bucket replication / cross-region config that might cause eventual consistency causing transient NoSuchKey responses? Check bucket config with infra.
- Confirm whether multipart uploads for these objects are finished and verified (ask release-eng).
- Add unit/integration tests for downloader to simulate partial reads and ensure atomic replace.

Links / artifacts:
- Jira: JIRA-INF-3421 (incident)
- PR I made to increase retries: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INF-3421

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Audit loader download code path for atomic tmp-file write and ensure truncation before write. (me)
- [ ] Add post-download head-object verify + checksum before moving into active dir. (me + Jordan)
- [ ] Run staged repro with 50 parallel downloads to validate flaky behaviour and gather S3 request/response traces. (Sofia)
- [ ] Kick off infra check on bucket replication and multipart upload history. (Infra)
